court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
trial_court: Court of Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate-VIII, Ghaziabad, Case No. 537 of 2016
case_name: Durgesh Nandan @ Durgesh Sharma vs State Of U.P. And Anr.

parties.respondent_defendant: State Of U.P. And Anr., Smt. Renu (wife)

facts_of_case: The parties entered into a compromise and the wife received Rs. 4 lakhs. The husband has filed this application to quash the proceedings under Section 498-A, 323, 504, 506, 406 IPC and Section 3/4 D.P. Act.

legal_principles.principle: Criminal proceedings may be quashed even in non-compoundable cases by the High Court in exercise of its extraordinary jurisdiction.
legal_principles.held: In all the aforesaid cases, the Apex Court has laid down the law that criminal proceedings may be quashed even in non-compoundable cases by the High Court in exercise of its extraordinary jurisdiction.
cited_cases: Gian Singh vs. State of Punjab, (2012), 10 SCC 303
B.S. Joshi and others vs. State of Haryana and another, (2003) 4 SCC 675
Madan Mohan Abbot vs. State of Punjab, (2008) 4 SCC 582

legal_principles.principle: Continuation of proceedings will be an abuse of process of law if the dispute has been settled amicably out of court.
legal_principles.held: At this stage, learned counsel for the applicant has also submitted that continuation of the proceedings of the aforesaid case will be an abuse of process of law.
cited_cases: Gian Singh vs. State of Punjab, (2012), 10 SCC 303
B.S. Joshi and others vs. State of Haryana and another, (2003) 4 SCC 675
Madan Mohan Abbot vs. State of Punjab, (2008) 4 SCC 582

outcome.final_order: The proceeding is quashed as the parties have settled their dispute amicably out of court.

use_for_drafting: quashing criminal proceedings in family disputes
summoning orders in domestic violence cases
